clue.text: In retirement, start to scoff an essential, like fruit

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from scoff
retiring means drawing back, so the opening pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: an essential is a must, something you cannot do without
as means like, in the way of

explanation.surface: Someone retiring treats themselves to a necessary snack of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retirement' turns S (start to scoff), A and MUST together, giving SATSUM; AS (like) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a small loose-skinned citrus, a type of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Scrubbing faces, L'Oreal have broadcast its benefits

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters that remain are thrown into a new order
a word's face is its front, so scrubbing faces wipes off the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A cosmetics advertiser, hiding the models' faces, airs the benefits of its product.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the first letters of L'OREAL and HAVE leaves OREAL and AVE; 'broadcast' rearranges OREALAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera gel is the plant extract whose soothing benefits skin-care adverts promote, so the clue's 'its' refers to that ingredient.

clue.text: By changing outgrowth, toe to head, animal could be this

indicators.note: changing signals that the word for outgrowth is altered by shifting one of its letters
the toe of a word is its last letter, which moves up to the front, its head

parts.note: horns are bony outgrowths on an animal's head

explanation.surface: A creature reshaping its horns and hooves into a strange form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toe to head' takes the final S of HORNS and puts it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep that has been clipped of its fleece is said to be shorn.

clue.text: Style of underpants in Action Man involved crazy consumer warning

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the rearranged letters of the toy's name
involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters of Action Man are rearranged

parts.note: Y-fronts are a style of men's briefs, so Y names the style
nuts is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A toy soldier in odd underwear sparks an alarming safety notice.
explanation.walkthrough: Action Man is a British boy's action-figure toy; 'involved' rearranges its letters to MACONTAIN, and 'in' puts Y inside, after MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Food packaging carries this allergy notice to warn buyers that traces of peanuts or tree nuts might be present.

clue.text: Weapon old Asian boss keeps close to chest

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the boss's title contains the next piece

parts.note: a shogun was a hereditary military ruler of Japan before 1868

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from chest

explanation.surface: A Japanese warlord holds his arms tight against his chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' puts T, the last letter of chest, inside SHOGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-bore gun firing pellets is a firearm, a common weapon.

clue.text: Judge let off second suspect

indicators.note: let off means released or excused, so one letter is dropped from the word for second

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A judge acquits someone a moment after doubting the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The judge seems to be the one letting someone off; J for judge is actually what is removed from JIFFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dubious or questionable is informally called iffy.

clue.text: Cool beer stores best where chopped onions might go

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: stores means keeps inside, so the word for beer holds the word for best

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
the pick of something is its best part

explanation.surface: Chilled beer is the best thing to drink while making a pickle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a play: chopped onions might go into a pickle (vinegar preserve), and the phrase also means in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Onions are preserved in vinegar as pickled onions, so the jar is where they might go; the idiom itself means in a predicament.

clue.text: Uplifting service consumes the clergyman

indicators.note: consumes means swallows, so the service's letters go round the next word
in a down clue lifting up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: An inspiring church service absorbs the priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' points to a church service, but it is the RAF; 'uplifting' turns it to FAR, and 'consumes' puts THE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Father is the title used for a Catholic or Anglican priest.

clue.text: Note cost, travelling by air and rail, given a wide berth?

indicators.note: travelling suggests moving around, so the letters of note cost are rearranged

parts.note: to air a grievance is to vent it
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A traveller notes the cost of flying versus the train and decides to keep away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' rearranges NOTE COST to SENTTOCO; VENT and RY follow. 'By air and rail' looks like transport, but air is VENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ostracised, ignored by everyone, is to be shunned, which the question mark likens to being given a wide berth.

clue.text: Marco joins some chopping a sausage

parts.note: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller

indicators.note: chopping means cutting off, so a letter is removed from the word for some

parts.note: any can mean some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: The explorer Marco joins a group cutting up a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: MARCO points to POLO, the Venetian explorer; 'chopping a' removes A from ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Polony is a large, finely minced, ready-cooked pork sausage, popular in South Africa and Britain.

clue.text: Ham and eggs sustain royal court

indicators.note: sustain means hold up, so the eggs hold the royal piece within

parts.note: ova is Latin for eggs
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A breakfast of ham and eggs keeps the royal household going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like food beside eggs; it is the verb to overplay a part.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor who hams it up overplays, exaggerating a performance.

clue.text: Electronic game one disallowed, heading for general prayers

indicators.note: disallowed means not permitted, so a letter is struck out of the word for game

parts.note: venison is game meat from deer
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, taken from general

explanation.surface: An electronic game is ruled out, leading people to general prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests something played; it is game meat, VENISON, losing I.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening service of prayer, sung at dusk.

clue.text: Ladies perhaps work and rest alternately

parts.note: toil is hard work

indicators.note: alternately means every other letter is taken from rest

explanation.surface: Advice to divide your day between labour and rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of rest give ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies is the name on a women's public lavatory, an example of a convenience.

clue.text: Polish bird, in fiction, picked up novel

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so the pieces are said aloud

parts.note: to polish is to brighten; the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A Polish bird appears in a story someone overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb. Brighton is an English seaside resort; Brighton rock is its seaside candy and Graham Greene's 1938 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's 1938 crime book about a gang in a seaside town is a famous English novel.

clue.text: Order masks etc for 1970s film

indicators.note: masks means covers or hides, so the order's name surrounds the next piece

parts.note: the Garter is the senior order of British chivalry
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to cover things and so on, for a film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' suggests a command; it is the Order of the Garter, which 'masks' (holds) ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Get Carter is a 1971 British gangster movie starring Michael Caine.

clue.text: Bedroom includes shower that is comparatively smart

indicators.note: includes means contains, so the bedroom abbreviation goes round the other pieces

parts.note: BR is the estate agents' abbreviation for bedroom
rain is a shower
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An en-suite bedroom with a shower is the cleverer choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' suggests a bathroom fitting; it is a shower of RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: More intelligent is the comparative of clever, matching a smarter person.

clue.text: Maths department ignore Tom struggling with test

indicators.note: struggling suggests twisting about, so the letters of ignore Tom are rearranged

parts.note: to try is to test

explanation.surface: A maths student called Tom gives up struggling with an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' rearranges IGNORE and TOM into TRIGONOME.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of mathematics dealing with triangles and angles is a department of maths.

clue.text: According to T. Emin or other, how Turner Prize is won?

indicators.note: other means different, so the letters of T Emin and or are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist, Tracey Emin or someone else, wonders how the Turner Prize is won.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a British artist shortlisted for the Turner Prize, Britain's best-known contemporary-art award; 'other' rearranges T EMIN OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning because of the quality of one's work is winning by merit, the hoped-for basis of an arts award.

clue.text: Hardy perennial alongside this buddy tree

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a tough plant and its companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel was the film partner of Oliver Hardy, always beside him; 'Hardy perennial' looks like gardening but names the comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner in the duo; the bay is an evergreen shrub or tree of the same name.

clue.text: Advanced wide probes to capture knight

indicators.note: probes means pushes into, so the two letters go inside the word for capture

parts.note: to gain is to win or capture
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
W is the abbreviation for wide, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A forward attack goes wide in an attempt to capture a knight on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Probes' puts AW inside GAIN. Gawain is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain is one of Arthur's Round Table knights, famed from the Green Knight poem.

clue.text: Outsiders in Marathon come in, rousing jogger?

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters, taken from marathon
rousing means stirring up, so the letters of come in are rearranged

explanation.surface: The runners at the back of a marathon come in, stirring the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' suggests a runner; it is something that jogs the memory. 'Rousing' rearranges COME IN to EMONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory aid such as a rhyme jogs the memory, so it is a jogger of recall.

clue.text: Suppose a couple of pints will go down in one

indicators.note: in a down clue going down in means being placed inside the word below
a couple means two, so the first two letters are taken from pints

explanation.surface: A drinker imagines two pints being downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go down in one' suggests downing a drink; PI, the first two letters of pints, goes inside ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state a view, to suppose or think.

clue.text: It goes round and round, similarly forward and back

indicators.note: reading the same forward and back means the answer is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A description of a wheel that turns both ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a device or muscle that turns something about an axis, spinning repeatedly.

clue.text: Small beer Victoria ordered, avoiding constant round

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the remaining letters are put in a new order
avoiding means leaving out, so two letters are dropped from Victoria

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Victoria orders a half pint but skips the next round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small beer' looks like a drink order; it means trifles. Removing C and O from VICTORIA leaves VITRIA, which 'ordered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is an idiom for unimportant matters, trifles and inconsequential details.

clue.text: It's hard to see this rock band

explanation.surface: A band so loud and fast you can't make it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A smudge or haze is something indistinct and hard to make out; Blur were a 1990s British Britpop group.

clue.text: Live in Scottish town, employed in sample Scottish plant

indicators.note: employed in means put to work inside, so the built piece goes inside the word for sample

parts.note: to try is to sample

indicators.note: in places the word for live inside the town's name

parts.note: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Someone living in a Scottish town samples a local fruit plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts BE inside AYR, giving AYBER, and 'employed in' puts that inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The tayberry is a raspberry-blackberry hybrid bred in Scotland and named after the River Tay.
